projects.title: The Notwork
projects.description: Production edtech platform where North Carolina high schoolers learn, play, and compete in STEM and skilled-trades programs.
projects.longDescription: The Notwork is the full-stack platform behind North Carolina's first state-backed esports and STEM league. Students learn through mastery pathways, play games, earn micro-credentials, and compete on rosters and leaderboards. The same platform runs the league: teachers verify students, staff manage content and seasons, and admins push updates all year. I co-architected it, led the team that built it and its 2025 rebuild, and have run it on my own since October 2025.
projects.role: Co-architect · led the build team · sole maintainer since Oct 2025
highlights: One of two architects who set the platform's direction. Led five developers through the initial build: hired the team, set coding standards and tooling, reviewed PRs weekly, and refined tickets with product and design.
Led the 2025 rebuild on a new architecture: schema redesign, end-to-end notifications, server pagination, error handling and logging, and hundreds of regression tests.
Designed identity verification for in-person competition: a teacher-as-verifier workflow, roster and eligibility logic, and team locking at playoff cutoffs, replacing manual spreadsheet checks.
AI-assisted judging: the model scores a submission against each rubric criterion with written reasoning and drafts feedback, and staff review and adjust it before saving.
Built mastery pathways with submissions, rubrics, AI-assisted grading, and micro-credentials, plus an Explore feed that mixes lessons, video, games, and submissions.
projects.problem: The league needed one platform that could both teach students and run the season: learning content, games, and competition for students, plus verification, rosters, communication, and content tools for teachers and staff.
projects.solution: A full-stack Next.js platform with role-based experiences for students, teachers, and staff. Students engage through pathways, games, and competitions; staff get admin tooling, content management, verification, messaging, and analytics in one place.
projects.impact: Replaced spreadsheets and ad-hoc tools with one production system that runs the league day to day: ~24K users, ~490K page views, and a peak of ~1K daily active users.

projects.title: AI Curriculum Pipeline
projects.description: A nine-step AI pipeline, with a human review point at every step, that turns a rough lesson idea into a published, multi-modal lesson in 10–30 minutes.
projects.longDescription: An applied-AI pipeline built into The Notwork that produces complete lessons. It runs nine steps modeled on real curriculum development: blueprint, outline, content, editorialize, accuracy check, media, formatting, audio, and release. Each step builds on the last, runs on the model the educator picks from Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google, and can be refined or regenerated before the lesson publishes straight to the platform.
highlights: Modeled the pipeline on how curriculum teams actually build lessons, so each step has one job and a clear output.
Model choice per step across Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google (Claude, GPT, and Gemini), including Gemini image generation for lesson media.
Human-in-the-loop by design: each step takes the previous output as context, and an educator can refine or regenerate it before it feeds the next.

An editorial step scores tone and readability and proposes line edits as before-and-after diffs; an accuracy step checks each factual claim with a confidence score and flags what needs subject-matter review.
Generated images wait for an educator to approve or regenerate them, then upload to the Cloudflare CDN and are written into the lesson.
Each finished lesson ships with text-to-speech narration and practice questions.
projects.problem: Curriculum production was slow and inconsistent. A single quality lesson could take a week by hand, and the platform needed a steady stream of multi-modal content for students.
projects.solution: A nine-step pipeline that walks an educator from rough requirements to a published, multi-modal lesson, with refine and regenerate controls at every step and direct publishing into The Notwork.
projects.impact: Cut lesson production from about a week to 10–30 minutes, with higher consistency than the manual process. 55 lessons published so far.

projects.title: Skilled-Trades Games
projects.description: Ten playable browser games that teach skilled-trades work through short, scored scenarios. Built solo in Pixi.js and Three.js.
projects.longDescription: A suite of browser games built for a skilled-trades workforce program on The Notwork. They cover construction sequencing, electrical, plumbing and HVAC, site safety, and tool fluency, from 2D puzzles in Pixi.js to a 3D isometric job site in Three.js. Each game is short and scored, with levels and progression, so it works as standalone practice or as league content.
highlights: Designed and built every game end to end, with no prior game-development background.
Used AI-assisted workflows for scoping, programmatically generated assets, and fast iteration.
Each game has scoring, levels, and progression, and works as standalone practice or league content.
features: Scoring, levels, and unlock progression in every game
2D puzzle and arcade games in Pixi.js
A 3D isometric job-site inspection in Three.js (Site Audit)
Diagnose-and-fix service calls with a customer story (Circuit Breaker, Flow State)
Practice modes alongside scored runs in several games
Phone-first layouts that also work on desktop

projects.title: CTAC — Careers in Technology Cohort
projects.description: Ran a software-careers program for adults: wrote the curriculum, taught it daily, and placed 100+ graduates of my first two cohorts in full-time roles.
projects.longDescription: CTAC was an intensive careers-in-technology program for adults moving into software. I went through the program as a student, then came back as a co-founder and its Director of Curriculum and Programming. I wrote the curriculum, taught it daily as the sole instructor for two years, supervised a third, and worked with corporate sponsors so each cohort learned what their hiring pipelines needed.
projects.role: Co-founder & Director of Curriculum and Programming
highlights: 100+ graduates of the first two cohorts I taught were placed in full-time roles at Charlotte's major employers, including Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Lowe's, Ally, Coca-Cola Consolidated, and Truist.
Had a direct hand in training ~200 adults pursuing software careers across three years of cohorts.
Led a four-person curriculum team on a contracted cohort build for an external client.
Worked with corporate sponsors so cohorts launched with the curriculum their hiring pipelines needed.

projects.title: hector-mono
projects.description: My public monorepo: this site, a recipes app, a bookmarks app, and an AI tools catalog, on a shared component library with strict CI.
projects.longDescription: A Turborepo monorepo where I build in public. It holds this portfolio, a recipes app with sign-in and a Postgres database, Stash for bookmarks, and a catalog of AI and web tools built on the AI SDK. The apps share a shadcn/ui-based component package, the backend apps follow clean-architecture layers that lint rules enforce, and CI runs lint, typecheck, and tests on every pull request.
highlights: Clean-architecture layers in the backend apps, enforced by lint rules rather than convention.
A shared design system: shadcn/ui components with a lint layer that fails CI on off-system colors and styles.
Every pull request runs lint, typecheck, and tests for the packages it touches.
